title: Porsche to continue with Wehrlein and Müller for GEN4
excerpt:
With the GEN4 era fast approaching, the reigning Manufacturers' Champions have opted for consistency in their driver line-up.

As one of the most successful teams in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship, Porsche know what it takes to win. Following a dominant stretch that brought driver and manufacturer world titles back to Germany, Porsche is locking in continuity behind the wheel for the championship's most exciting era to date.

Capable of reaching speeds in excess of 335kph, 0-100kph in approximately 1.8 seconds, and 0-200kph in just 4.4 seconds - 1.5 seconds faster than its predecessor - GEN4 will deliver 50% more power in race mode than the current GEN3 Evo race car. The GEN4 car will be an average of 10 seconds faster per lap than the GEN3 car in qualifying mode. In ATTACK MODE, GEN4 produces up to 600kW of power, a 71% increase in base output over GEN3 Evo, delivering performance that pushes the limits of electric racing. GEN4 is the only single-seater race car with permanent all-wheel drive.

Despite some ups and downs along the way, Wehrlein's 2025/26 Formula E season culminated in a masterclass of consistency and speed as he claimed his second Drivers' World Championship with the Porsche outfit. On the path to his coronation, Wehrlein recorded three E-Prix victories and secured six podium finishes - results which established his position as a championship protagonist throughout the season.

Meanwhile, Müller's 2025/26 campaign with Porsche marked a career-defining breakthrough, as the Swiss driver proved to be a critical asset alongside teammate Wehrlein. Over the course of the season, he delivered some impressive performances, including a second-place at the Miami E-Prix and a dominant victory at the Berlin E-Prix in front of Porsche's jubilant home crowd.

With a proven champion in Wehrlein and proven race winner in Müller behind-the-wheel, the German squad has locked in an impressive line-up to defend their crowns and dominate the fastest, most exciting chapter in the world's leading all-electric championship.

title: From heartbreak to history: Pascal Wehrlein’s journey to two-time Formula E Champion
excerpt:
11 Wins, 24 Podiums, 2 Titles: the defining Formula E career highlights of Pascal Wehrlein

In one of the most unpredictable finishes in Formula E history, Pascal Wehrlein clinched his second Drivers' World Championship, as a nine-driver title battle came down to the final moments of the season in London.

Across his eight-year career in the all-electric series - and three generations of Formula E machinery - the German-Mauritian driver has achieved 11 victories, 24 podiums, and 883 laps led.

We take a look back at some of his Formula E highlights and uncover what truly makes him a champion.

The move to Mahindra

His success as the youngest driver to win the DTM championship opened the door to Formula 1, where he debuted with Manor Racing in 2016, before moving to Sauber the following year, for what would be his final season in the championship. However, after briefly returning to DTM in 2018, he transitioned to Formula E with Mahindra Racing, joining the team on the first day of 2018/19 pre-season testing in Valencia.

When the season got underway, Wehrlein immediately impressed, scoring his first-ever Formula E podium in just the third round of the season at the 2019 Santiago E-Prix. In the following round, he also came painfully close to clinching his maiden victory in a chaotic Mexico City E-Prix.

The German driver secured his maiden pole and led the field for the majority of the race, with Oliver Rowland and Lucas di Grassi breathing down his neck and applying pressure. He fought hard, but di Grassi wouldn’t give him a moment’s respite. Heading into the final lap in front of almost 40,000 fans, Wehrlein ran out of energy heading out of the final turn, allowing the Brazilian to slip through and cross the line first.

He finished his rookie season on 58 points, just nine points behind his then more senior teammate, Jerome d’Ambrosio. The partnership would continue to the following season, where he finished 18th on the standings, with fourth place as his best result.

Triumph in Mexico

Wehrlein would soon find a home with TAG Heuer Porsche for the 2020/21 Formula E season. His first campaign with the German automotive giant was a story of missed opportunities, with technical infringements costing both him and the team a potential maiden victory at the 2021 Puebla E-Prix, despite Wehrlein crossing the line first after starting from pole position. The following day brought further frustration: Wehrlein finished second but was demoted to fourth after a five-second penalty for improper use of FANBOOST.

Heading into the following season, Wehrlein had plenty to prove. Having being denied victory in Mexico City twice, the 2022 E-Prix finally offered a different ending. Starting from pole position, he initially led the race before dropping behind Edoardo Mortara and Jean-Eric Vergne as the leading group battled for position. Rather than forcing his way through prematurely, Wehrlein focused on energy efficiency, keeping enough in reserve to attack when it mattered most.

With 15 minutes on the clock, Wehrlein and then teammate Andre Lotterer, made their move, passing Vergne and then Mortara, to reclaim the lead of the race with a comfortable nine second gap to their rivals. Wehrlein then controlled the closing stages, with Lotterer following him across the line to complete a historic one-two finish. It was Wehrlein’s first Formula E win and Porsche’s first in the all-electric championship since entering the series in 2019.

Two victories within 24 hours

The beginning of the GEN3 era saw Wehrlein firmly established as a title contender. After finishing second behind Andretti’s Jake Dennis in the Mexico City season opener, he arrived in Diriyah ready to fight back.

The Saudi Arabian double-header would become one of the defining weekends of his Formula E career.

Qualifying for the first race proved challenging, leaving the Porsche driver ninth on the grid. But while others fought for position through the opening corners, he made up ground quickly, navigating the early chaos and working his way into the top six. He then timed his ATTACK MODE activations effectively, using the additional power to move through the field while preserving enough energy for the closing stages.

The decisive move came on Lap 30 at Turn 16, when Wehrlein passed Jaguar’s Sam Bird for the lead. From there, he had to withstand pressure from championship leader Jake Dennis, who had also fought his way through the pack. Wehrlein managed his energy and pace superbly to hold off the Andretti driver and secure his first win of the season.

Just 24 hours later, Wehrlein returned to the grid in fifth, with Dennis starting sixth. Once again, the German driver demonstrated that qualifying position would not dictate his afternoon. He made up places early, remained patient as the leaders cycled through their ATTACK MODE activations, and waited for the right moment to strike.

As the leading group reshuffled, Wehrlein seized the advantage and moved into the lead, with Dennis once again emerging as his closest challenger. The Porsche driver held firm through the closing laps to claim his second consecutive victory, which promoted him to the top of the Driver’s Championship - granting Porsche an early advantage in the title fight.

Despite this impressive start to the season, Wehrlein ultimately finished fourth in Drivers' standings with 149 points, adding two further victories to his tally and consistently finishing inside the top-10.

2023/24 Season finale: Wehrlein vs Evans

The 2023/24 season was Wehrlein’s strongest campaign yet. He opened the season with victories in Mexico and Misano and maintained his consistency throughout the year. However, despite his strong form, the title fight went down to the wire, with the London E-Prix double-header set to decide the championship.

Wehrlein started third on the grid, while Mitch Evans stormed away from pole position. It took Wehrlein 16 laps to find the perfect opportunity to slip past Envision Racing’s Sebastian Buemi and take the lead from the Jaguar TCS Racing driver, making the most out of his ATTACK MODE. He held on to secure his third victory of the season, but the title fight was far from over, with Wehrlein holding just a three-point advantage over Evans on 177 points. ,

The final round delivered the expected drama. Nick Cassidy kicked off from pole, with Evans starting third and Wehrlein fourth. The equation was simple: whichever contender finished ahead of the other would have a crucial advantage in the title fight.

By Lap 11, Evans was still looking strong, but Wehrlein was breathing down his neck, with both drivers running near the front of the pack. The turning point came when contact involving Cassidy and Antonio Felix da Costa damaged the Jaguar driver’s hopes of securing the title, leaving Evans and Wehrlein to fight for the crown.

Wehrlein ultimately crossed the line second behind Oliver Rowland, with Evans finishing third. Despite not winning the race, the result was enough to secure the Drivers’ World Championship for Wehrlein, who finished the season on 198 points, just six ahead of Evans.

Champions are made under pressure

Fast forward to the 2025/26 Formula E season finale in London, and Wehrlein arrived at the British capital just five points behind championship leader Jake Dennis and three points behind second-placed Mitch Evans, leaving everything to play for in the final two rounds.

The 31-year-old driver delivered when it mattered most, taking victory from pole position in the penultimate race after making all the right decisions. He crossed the line five seconds ahead of Dennis, setting up a final showdown between the pair in the final race of the GEN3 era.

READ MORE: Best final lap drama from the 2025/26 Formula E season

The final qualifying session of the year proved successful for Wehrlein, as he lined up third on the grid, while Evans started fifth and Dennis could only manage 16th. It was a difficult position for the Andretti driver, but Evans was still eyeing his long-awaited championship crown. For Evans, the equation was simple: he needed to win, and hope that Wehrlein finished outside the points. And as the race unfolded, things began to fall into place for the Jaguar driver - could he do the impossible?

In the race, Wehrlein dropped out of the top five and gradually slipped to 11th, while Evans moved ahead of his teammate, da Costa, to climb to fourth. The Jaguar drivers also had another target in sight, with the team fighting to secure its second Teams’ Championship. With just two laps remaining, contact involving Dennis and Wehrlein disrupted both drivers’ races. Although both managed to return to the track, there was little time left to make up the lost ground.

Evans ultimately finished fourth, but it was not enough to overturn Wehrlein’s advantage in the standings. The German had done enough to claim his second Drivers’ World Championship, while Porsche also secured the Manufacturers’ Title.

Heading into GEN4 as our reigning champion, what's next for Pascal Wehrlein?

title: Gerry Hughes announced as Deputy Team Principal at Lola Formula E
excerpt:
The announcement comes as Lola reveals it will compete as the Lola Formula E team next season, with Yamaha continuing its role as technical partner.

Bringing with him a wealth of motorsport experience across both Formula E and Formula 1 - including serving as Team Principal of the NIO Formula E Team - Hughes will lead all operations and sporting matters while overseeing the day-to-day running of the Lola Formula E Team.

The appointment marks a return to Lola for Hughes, who was not only its Head of F1 Engineering in 2009 but also carried out his MSc research thesis on suspension design with the company.

Gerry Hughes, Deputy Team Principal, Lola Formula E, said: “Having worked for Lola on two previous occasions, the opportunity to re-join the prestigious British marque is something of a home coming for me and one that I take great pride in. Joining Lola also marks the third time I have worked alongside Mark Preston and Peter McCool, so there are a number of familiarities which will help me hit the ground running. Formula E has certainly come a long way technologically since I bowed out at the end of Season 5 and I am excited to be returning to the championship as it enters this new era.”

In further news, the team has revealed that for the upcoming 2026/27 Formula E season, they will compete as the 'Lola Formula E Team'. This name change reflects Lola’s growing capabilities as an independent manufacturer, following the in-housing of the race team, with the team reaffirming that Yamaha will continue its role as technical partner.

Mishern Chetty, CEO, Lola Cars said: "Since the inception of Lola’s Formula E program Yamaha has been an invaluable technical partner, providing expertise and resource which has been key to our development. We are proud to be continuing this relationship with them for our GEN4 campaign, where they remain a core part of the team.

"The importance of our relationship with Yamaha was reflected through their inclusion in our team name and branding level in our initial seasons. However, following the decision to bring the race team in-house for GEN4 to streamline activities and increase expertise for future motorsport projects, we have updated our team name and positioning accordingly.

READ MORE: Everything you need to know about Formula E's all-new GEN4 era

The Lola squad finished last season 10th in the Teams' Championship on 35 points - the majority of the points tally coming from Lucas di Grassi's incredible victory at the 2026 Shanghai E-Prix.

The team will announce their 2026/27 driver line-up in due course.

title: "Finishing on a high": Sébastien Buemi reflects on his final Formula E weekend
excerpt:
Sebastien Buemi called time on his illustrious Formula E career (for now) after the 2026 London E-Prix, with his future in the all-electric championship now set to take a different direction.

The 37-year-old Swiss driver has been a mainstay of the Formula E paddock since its inaugural season in 2014, and is one of only four drivers to have raced in every season, alongside Antonio Felix da Costa, Jean-Eric Vergne, and Lucas di Grassi.

He finishes his Formula E career with 160 starts, 14 victories, 36 podiums, and one Drivers’ Championship title, which he won in the 2015/16 season. He also remains in the Formula E history book as the most successful driver at the Monaco E-Prix, with three wins in 2015, 2017, and 2025 - one more than the only two-time victor, Oliver Rowland.

A permanent place within the Paysafe Envision family

Buemi joined Paysafe Envision Formula E (previously Envision Racing) at the start of the 2022/23 season, finishing sixth in the Drivers’ Championship that year, whilst his third-place finish in the London E-Prix season finale helped the British team secure its first and, as of the end of the 2025/26 campaign, only Teams’ Championship.

READ MORE: Paysafe Envision reveal new livery for 2026/27 Formula E season

The following year, Buemi finished 15th in the standings, but again ended the year on a high with a podium in London, his second trip to the rostrum in the 2023/24 season. 2024/25's campaign gave Buemi his long-awaited 14th Formula E victory, after winning the Monaco E-Prix for the third time - solidifying his status as the all-electric 'Mr Monaco'.

This season, however, was one of highs and lows for Buemi, who entered the London finale with 75 championship points and only one podium finish from the season, despite a relatively consistent run of finishes inside the top- ten.

At the London E-Prix double-header, the final race weekend of the 2025/26 season and the last races of the GEN3 era, he impressed in Saturday's race, starting from P10 and using the Full Course Yellow period to his advantage as both Lola Yamaha ABT’s drivers, Zane Maloney and Lucas di Grassi, ended up in the wall. Though he narrowly missed out on a podium, he managed to take home fourth whilst his teammate Joel Eriksson finished 14th.

Reflecting on the race, he said, “I always do the best I can, and then move on, no more special feeling.” He continued, “I’m happy to score a few points. Obviously, Saturday was a crazy race, like it is always here in London.

“I'm lucky with the strategy, we pitted under the Full Course Yellow, but at the same time, I had the ATTACK MODE, so I did lose a bit of hope. It feels like P3 would have been possible with the perfect race, but at the end of the day, I'm quite happy with that result.

“I always have a different mindset. We take it step by step, session by session. In this category, so many things can happen. I'm not too bothered. I just do the best I can and then at the end of the day we count whether we score points or not.”

Sunday’s race was chaotic, to say the least, with much of the attention focused on the three championship protagonists. Porsche’s Pascal Wehrlein ultimately came out on top of Andretti’s Jake Dennis and Jaguar TCS Racing’s Mitch Evans, securing his second World Championship title.

READ MORE: Pascal Wehrlein wins his second Formula E Drivers' World Championship

Amidst the chaos, Buemi kept his cool. On Lap 13, he activated his four-minute ATTACK MODE, which helped him climb to P6. His teammate Eriksson made contact with the reigning champion on the same lap, forcing him out of the race. Buemi, meanwhile, continued to fight at the front and held on to claim fifth in his final appearance behind-the-wheel of the GEN3 car with the Envision squad.

“I don't think I could have done much better, so I'm happy with that result," he said. "Finishing on a high, quite a few points, 22 points this weekend. So I feel like I've done my job.”

“It's much better than having a DNF or a bad race. I don't think it would have changed much anyway, but at least to finish on the high and having done a good race, scoring nearly 100 points this season. It could have been better, but it's not that bad.”

What the future has in store

Buemi's success behind-the-wheel extends beyond the Formula E paddock, the Swiss driver has won four World Endurance Championship Drivers’ titles, in 2014, 2019, 2022 and 2023, and has claimed four overall victories at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, in 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2022.

With such a prestigious racing CV, there is little doubt that the Swiss driver has a bright future in store - wherever he ends up.

“I guess I'll digest a little bit, the fact that I'm not going to be racing next year," he says. "And then at some point, just really discuss what we can do to get involved with the team and how I can contribute.

“We will do that in the next few weeks and see how we can obviously approach the next season. I'm going to stay in the team as an advisor. I wish I would have been able to continue, but of course there are a lot of things happening with the fact that we have so many races with WEC and it's the way it is.

“I’m wishing the team the very best, I might do a test from time to time, and I'm looking forward to seeing the car on track and hopefully it's going to look good on TV.”

title: Jaguar unveils its first next-gen EV: the Type 01
excerpt:
This week, at its global premiere in New York City, Jaguar gave the world a first look at the beginning of a dramatic new chapter with its all-electric grand tourer, the Type 01.

Now, we've had a complete look at the production model - the iconic British marque's first production car of its rebooted, all-electric era.

It is an ultra-luxury, zero-emission four-door GT with a blistering 0-62mph time of 3.2 seconds, powered by a tri-motor setup that generates an astonishing 1,030PS (1,016bhp) and 1,365Nm of torque.

How fast is the Jaguar Type 01, what's its range and how does it look?

The British manufacturer's new flagship promises up to 400 miles of EPA range (or 450 miles/720km WLTP) courtesy of its 118kWh usable battery pack.

Operating on an ultra-fast 850-volt electrical architecture, it can add 200 miles of range in just 13 minutes when hooked up to a 350kW rapid DC charger.

Built upon the bespoke Jaguar Electric Architecture (JEA), the platform allows for dramatic "exuberant modernist" proportions - featuring a low roofline, elongated bonnet, short front overhang, and massive 23-inch wheels - while maintaining ideal 50:50 weight distribution for sharp dynamic handling.

Drivers benefit from intelligent torque vectoring and active aerodynamics, including active vanes and a three-stage deployable rear spoiler that helps yield a sleek 0.23 drag coefficient.

Jaguar has ensured the Type 01 looks unlike anything else on the road, matching its exterior drama with a rich, tech-forward cabin.

Inside, a central longitudinal spine splits the cabin into four distinct zones, complemented by brass-effect anodised aluminium trim, a single glass 24-inch OLED Interactive Driver Display, a secondary 7-inch touchscreen console, and a full-width Panoramic Soundbar with sensory audio seats.

Type 01: Jaguar's charge into a modern luxury future

Nodding to the brand's heritage while signalling its clean-sheet reset, the "Type" designation honors legendary models like the E-Type, while "0" denotes zero emissions and "1" marks the first vehicle of its new generation.

Leveraging track-to-road engineering insights honed by the double world championship-winning Jaguar TCS Racing Formula E team, Jaguar’s electric power delivery has been calibrated to give deep reserves of rolling power, launching from 62mph to 112mph (100km/h to 180km/h) in just 4.0 seconds.

Designed, engineered, and manufactured in the UK, the Type 01 spearheads Jaguar's transition into a fully electric modern luxury brand. Order books for the four-door grand tourer are set to open in early 2027, with the first client deliveries scheduled for the second half of that year.

What does the Jaguar Type 01 cost and when can you buy one?

Positioning the electric GT firmly in high-end luxury territory, pricing for the Jaguar Type 01 starts from £130,000 ($130,500 in the US), with higher-spec and bespoke builds expected to reach beyond £150,000.

Order books for the British-built flagship are slated to open in early 2027, with first client deliveries scheduled to follow in the second half of the year.

title: COMSOL named Official Multiphysics Partner of Formula E
excerpt:
COMSOL and Formula E have announced a multi-year partnership naming COMSOL the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

The partnership brings together Formula E, the world’s leading all-electric motorsport Championship, and COMSOL, a global leader in multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering (CAE) software. Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics® to investigate complex technology challenges involving multiple interacting physical effects.

Electric race cars bring together electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid, and battery systems under extreme constraints. As Official Multiphysics Partner, COMSOL will support Formula E with simulation software and expertise to help its technology teams understand how interacting physical phenomena influence multiple aspects of the sport. The partnership will also explore how simulation apps and digital twin solutions can make physics-based insight accessible beyond the traditional modeling workflow.

Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said: “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another. We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”

Dan Cherowbrier, CTO at Formula E, said: “Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modeling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing.”

Looking ahead, the next generation of Formula E will place even greater demands on performance, efficiency, energy management, and vehicle development as the Championship prepares for the GEN4 era, introducing the fastest and most technologically advanced race car to date.

At the same time, COMSOL has announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, scheduled for release later this autumn, with new capabilities particularly relevant to advanced engineering workflows, including dedicated electric motor modeling, system-level simulation, agentic modeling, and expanded access for creating simulation apps.

The partnership was announced today at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston, where Cherowbrier delivered a keynote talk on the technology and engineering shaping the future of Formula E. To learn more about the partnership, visit COMSOL's website: www.comsol.com/formula-e.

title: Opel GSE unveils new livery for 2026/27 Formula E season

title: Every Formula E Driver Who Has Won Their Home E-Prix
excerpt:
Feature by Katy Fairman

Across 12 seasons of Formula E, only a select few can say they’ve been victorious on home soil. Winning your home event is a special – and rare – achievement, and often a dream for most drivers, but how often has that happened in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship?

From nerve-wracking overtakes on iconic city streets to emotional maiden victories, a select group of drivers have overcome the immense pressure of their home crowds to take the chequered flag. Here are the elite Formula E drivers who delivered unforgettable victories on home turf.

Jake Dennis in London (2021 and 2022)

Standing on the top step at your home race is a rare feat, but Andretti’s Jake Dennis has managed it twice and is the only person on this list to do so.

During the London E-Prix in both the 2020/21 and 2021/22 seasons, Dennis dominated the opening race of both double-headers. In 2021, he converted a front-row start into a decisive victory, finishing over five seconds clear of Nyck de Vries. The following year, Dennis delivered a commanding lights-to-flag win over Stoffel Vandoorne, then backed it up with a second-place finish the next day on London's unique indoor-outdoor circuit.

While he missed out on a hat-trick of London wins in 2022/23, Dennis clinched the Drivers’ World Championship at the ExCeL London instead—becoming the first British driver in Formula E history to secure the crown on home soil.

Jean-Eric Vergne in Paris (2018)

Citroën Racing’s Jean-Éric Vergne claimed a memorable home victory during the 2018 Paris E-Prix. Starting from pole position, the Frenchman kept his composure on the streets of Paris, fending off Sam Bird and André Lotterer through mid-race car swaps to secure the win with the Eiffel Tower in the background.

Calling it the "most emotional" victory of his career, Vergne admitted he couldn't even speak as he crossed the finish line. The win was a special birthday milestone in a dominant year that saw him go on to claim his first Drivers' Championship.

Vergne repeated his title glory in the following season, making him the only back-to-back champion in Formula E history. Très bien, JEV!

Taylor Barnard in London (2026)

The most recent addition to this list is Taylor Barnard, who became Formula E’s youngest-ever winner when he took his maiden victory at the final race of the 2025/26 in London.

Surrounded by friends and family, the young Briton was able to pass both Mahindra’s as the race drew to a close and added his name into the record books as the World Championship’s youngest winner aged 22 years, two months and 15 days. Racing for DS PENSKE, Barnard’s silverware also meant that all teams recorded at least one podium result and all but one team achieved a victory across the season.

Maximilian Guenther in Berlin (2020)

During the 2019/20 campaign, Maximilian Guenther claimed a thrilling victory on home soil at the Berlin E-Prix while driving for BMW i Andretti Motorsport.

Competing at the Tempelhof Airport circuit, Guenther executed a daring pass on Jean-Éric Vergne for the lead with just four minutes remaining. Ignoring team instructions to wait until the final lap, the German made the move stick to secure his second career Formula E win.

The tense victory showcased his huge potential, and Guenther has since added five more wins – seven total – to his resume, most recently taking top honors at the 2025 Shanghai E-Prix for DS PENSKE but moves to Paysafe Envision Racing for GEN4.

Sam Bird in London (2015)

Having been a part of Formula E since its inaugural season, Sam Bird has had plenty of opportunities to lock in a home win. Nevertheless, he didn't need it, as he won the London E-Prix in Formula E's very first season.

Navigating himself around the picturesque Battersea Park in England's capital, Bird won the final round of Season 1 in 2015. Repping Virgin Racing at the time, the Briton - born not at all far away in Roehampton - ended his maiden season on a high.

“What a way to finish [the season],” Bird said at the time. “Unbelievable, unbelievable. The race today was a great race, starting from fourth. We were very strong and I was able to attack people into Turn 11, and we made the moves stick which is nice.”

Oliver Rowland in London (2024)

Prior to his London win in 2024, Oliver Rowland had never scored a single point at a home E-Prix.

After missing the penultimate round in Portland due to illness, Rowland was out of championship contention, allowing him to race without pressure. He stayed patient in the lead group, capitalising as the title contenders battled around him to swoop ahead and cross the line first.

The breakthrough home win proved to be a sign of things to come, setting the stage for Rowland to go on and claim the 2024/25 Drivers' World Championship.

Daniel Abt in Berlin (2018)

Audi Sport ABT Schaeffler's Daniel Abt was on a mission during 2018’s race around Berlin’s historic Tempelhof Airport Circuit. Having achieved his maiden victory four races before in Mexico City, Abt was ready to repeat his success at his and Audi's home race.

Abt signed off a career-defining race weekend with a commanding lights-to-flag win on home soil at the popular venue. He also claimed pole position and the fastest lap – a then-unique feat in Formula E.

As well as Abt’s first place, his teammate Lucas di Grassi, was able to finish in second making it an Audi 1-2 result at their home event.

Alex Lynn in London (2021)

Representing Mahindra Racing, Alex Lynn secured a memorable home victory during the 2021 London E-Prix double-header, following Jake Dennis' win the previous day.

After finishing third on Saturday, Lynn took the top step just 24 hours later, earning his first and only victory in Formula E. Four years after earning pole position on his debut in New York City, the Briton finally tasted champagne on home soil at the Excel Arena.

The emotional breakthrough sparked wild celebrations in the pit lane, with Team Principal Dilbagh Gill famously leaping for joy as Lynn crossed the chequered flag to complete back-to-back British wins.

title: Bridgestone announced as Formula E’s GEN4 Tyre Supplier
excerpt:
Bridgestone return to an FIA World Championship as part of a multi-year partnership with Formula E.

Formula E has today announced Bridgestone Corporation as the official tyre supplier for the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship starting from the 2026/27 Season.

The upcoming season will see the launch of Formula E’s next-generation GEN4 race car, setting a new global benchmark for speed, performance, and sustainability in electric motorsport. The announcement follows a joint launch event held yesterday in Rome, Italy, where leadership from Formula E, the FIA, and Bridgestone unveiled the new tyres alongside the GEN4 show car.

Delivering unprecedented acceleration (0–100 km/h in 1.8 seconds), 600kW (815bhp) of peak power, and permanent active All-Wheel Drive, the GEN4 machine is the fastest and most powerful car in Formula E history. Bridgestone will support this leap in performance by introducing its bespoke high-performance POTENZA tyre range tailored specifically for the demands of GEN4 racing.

To meet the extreme torque, power, and dynamic capabilities of the GEN4 car, Bridgestone has engineered the all-weather POTENZA GEN4 tyre. Designed for high grip, long-lasting durability, and adaptability across diverse city street circuits and road conditions worldwide, the tyre ensures wheel-to-wheel excitement throughout each race.

INTRODUCING THE TYPHOON TYRE

Additionally, Bridgestone introduced the POTENZA GEN4 for TYPHOON TYRE, a heavy-wet specification tyre engineered to deliver maximum grip and stability during severe rain conditions, ensuring continuous, safe, and exciting racing in all weather scenarios.

Aligned with Formula E’s commitment to environmental leadership, Bridgestone’s GEN4 tyre range incorporates 65% recycled and renewable materials. This includes carbon black derived from end-of-life tyre pyrolysis oil, silica sourced from rice husks, and natural rubber compliant with the Global Platform for Sustainable Natural Rubber (GPSNR) standards. Production utilises 100% renewable energy for heat and electricity, while freight operations leverage low-carbon logistics solutions in partnership with DHL.

As part of the multi-year partnership, Bridgestone will also act as the Official Race Title Sponsor for four major race weekends during the 2026/27 Season, including Mexico City, Berlin, Shanghai and the season finale in Tokyo.

WELCOMING BRIDGESTONE TO FORMULA E

“We are delighted to welcome Bridgestone to Formula E as our sole tyre supplier for the 2026/27 Season and beyond,” Jeff Dodds, CEO, Formula E said. “Combining rich motorsport heritage with cutting-edge sustainable innovation, Bridgestone is a fitting partner as we embark on this exciting new era. The GEN4 car represents the pinnacle of sustainable motorsport design, and we look forward to working with Bridgestone as we continue to redefine electric racing and lead the race for progress both on and off the track.”

Yasuhiro Morita, Global CEO and Representative Executive Officer, Bridgestone Corporation, added: “Our return to the FIA World Championship is a major challenge that embodies Bridgestone’s history of passion and innovation. Under our Mission ‘Serving Society with Superior Quality,’ we have continued to push the limits with an insatiable quest for performance and a sense of responsibility for a better future through motorsports activities. On the supreme stage of Formula E, we will further evolve the balance of performance and sustainability and pioneer a new future for mobility. Together with organisers, teams, drivers, partners, and fans, we look forward to creating a new future.”

“Bridgestone’s appointment as the sole tyre supplier for the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship marks an exciting new chapter as we enter the GEN4 era.” Marek Nawarecki, Senior Circuit Sport Director, FIA, continued. “The tyres will play a key role in delivering the performance and efficiency expected from this new generation of Formula E cars. Building on the collaboration already established during the development of the GEN4 tyres, we look forward to continuing this work with Bridgestone, Formula E and the teams to deliver tyres that meet the demanding requirements of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship and contribute to close, competitive racing for drivers and fans.

“We are truly delighted to showcase Bridgestone’s technology and passion to the world on the new stage of Formula E,” Hiroshi Imai, Executive Officer, CPO, Global Motorsports, Bridgestone Corporation, made as the final point. “In developing POTENZA GEN4, we pushed the limits of our technology to fully unlock the overwhelming performance of GEN4. In particular, the newly introduced POTENZA GEN4 for TYPHOON TYRE represents a symbolic evolution for the GEN4 era, enabling drivers to confidently take on even wet conditions. By supporting the dramatically evolved GEN4 from the ground up, we are also advancing initiatives toward carbon neutrality and resource circulation, striving to realise sustainable motorsports.”

title: Mahindra Racing retain Mortara and de Vries for GEN4

title: Heron Preston and Formula E partner to rethink motorsport fashion
excerpt:
Previewing at ComplexCon, the creative partnership connects material-led design and racing innovation with the ambition to shape the future of motorsport fashion through sustainable design, performance and materials.

The partnership is rooted in what both achieve through reuse: Preston turns recovered materials into desirable design, while Formula E turns recovered energy into racing performance. Through eX-Ray, textile waste becomes new fabric; through regenerative braking, energy is recovered and used again. Together, they bring that thinking to the future of motorsport fashion.

eX-Ray is Heron Preston’s concept for looking at every element of a product with “X-ray vision”, from the materials and how they are made to the people and processes behind them. Rather than simply selecting existing fabrics, eX-Ray takes a more considered approach to how materials are developed and used. For the Formula E preview, this means using recycled cotton made from pre-consumer factory off-cuts and production scraps, which are sorted, shredded and re-spun into new yarn before being developed into a heavyweight, tightly woven fabric.

With the ambition to shape the future of motorsport fashion, the partnership brings a championship-wide perspective to material-led design. It pairs Preston’s expertise in transforming existing materials with Formula E’s pursuit of innovation and resource efficiency, exploring how those approaches can shape products from the outset.

The partners will offer a first look at their direction at ComplexCon Los Angeles through an exploration of eX-Ray materials, alongside a GEN4 car featuring an exclusive Preston-designed livery.

WHY HERON PRESTON AND FORMULA E

Preston’s work has consistently explored the potential of overlooked materials. His 2016 UNIFORM project upcycled decommissioned New York City Department of Sanitation uniforms and second-hand garments. More recently, he transformed Mercedes-Benz crash-test airbags into garments that retained the material’s distinctive physical qualities.

Working with manufacturers, engineers and material specialists, Preston explores how design can give existing resources renewed purpose. Formula E brings a complementary approach through racing, using the track to advance electric technology, energy efficiency and material innovation.

Together, they intend to apply that thinking to motorsport fashion, considering fit, fabrication, durability and end of life alongside the qualities that make people want to wear and keep a product.

A FIRST LOOK AT COMPLEXCON

ComplexCon brings together communities across style, sneakers, art, music and innovation, making it a natural setting to introduce the partnership to audiences beyond motorsport.

The installation will present garments as a way to explore the possibilities of eX-Ray materials, alongside Preston’s GEN4 car livery. Bringing materials, process and design together, it offers an early view of the partnership’s thinking and the possibilities the partners intend to explore.

A LONG-TERM AMBITION

ComplexCon offers a preview of a wider programme that the partners hope will span across performance, fashion, fan merchandise, accessories and products made from upcycled materials drawn from the sport. They intend to explore how Preston’s design approach and Formula E’s materials and technical knowledge can inform each category, from rethinking everyday merchandise to finding new uses for components and materials beyond their life in racing.

The GEN4 car provides a tangible example of Formula E’s approach. Designed to be 100% recyclable or reusable, with at least 20% recycled materials across key components, it demonstrates how performance and sustainability can be developed together. Formula E is also the world’s first Global B Corp Certified sport.

Heron Preston said: “This creative partnership is about rethinking what motorsport fashion can be. I’ve always been interested in taking materials, processes and ideas from unexpected places and finding new ways to give them purpose. Working with Formula E gives me the opportunity to bring that approach into a world where performance is everything. We’re looking at how apparel can be thoughtfully designed from the material up, balancing function, quality and a more considered approach to how things are made.”

title: Citroën Racing announce Team Principal and share GEN4 livery
excerpt:
Beth Paretta will become Citroën Racing’s Team Principal, with Frederic Espinos also joining the management structure, as the team share details of their new GEN4 livery ahead of the next chapter for the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

After supporting the team as Managing Director throughout its first season, Beth Paretta has been appointed Citroën Racing’s Team Principal for the 2026/27 Formula E season. She’ll be joined by Fred Espinos, who was previously Deputy Team Principal at the Lola Yamaha ABT squad.

The confirmation of a new Team Principal for Citroën Racing comes after the tragic passing of Cyril Blais – a highly-respected and well-loved member of the all-electric championship – who previously held that role within the team.

Blais’ death was felt far and wide across Formula E, and motor racing, with the championship commemorating his life over the Tokyo double-header event earlier this year, where Nick Cassidy was able to achieve two back-to-back podiums for the team in his honour.

Alongside this management structure reshuffle, the team proudly showed off its new look for the next chapter of Formula E, with the team still sticking to that iconic red, white and blue that was so-loved by fans in the 2025/26 campaign.

Citroën’s new GEN4 livery

Pierre Leclercq, Head of Citroën Design, explains, the objective of the new livery was to “retain the strong identity developed last season while adapting it to the more dynamic character of GEN4.” The more metallic finishes have also been designed so that “the car truly comes to life when it catches the light”, while the gradient is based on a parametric use of the chevrons, whose density progressively changes between the different shades.

Earlier this month, the team announced they were reuniting with TotalEnergies in GEN4 – a collaboration between two automotive giants that dates back to 1968, with particular success in rallying. Since 1968, Citroën and TotalEnergies have evolved side by side, both on the road and in competition, united by a shared culture of innovation, performance and the pursuit of excellence. This pairing now extends into their newest project: Formula E.

Beth Paretta on becoming Citroën’s Team Principal

For Paretta, who brings extensive motorsport experience spanning team management, the automotive industry and sporting governance, the GEN4 era brings new opportunities.

“GEN4 is much more than an evolution of the previous car: it is faster, more powerful and technologically more advanced, and it will change the way we approach race weekends,” Paretta stated. “For Citroën Racing, success will be about making the most of that opportunity from the very beginning.

“We feel well prepared, we have the strength and expertise of Stellantis Motorsport behind us, and we have a brand that is fully committed to the programme. Our objective is to translate all of that into being competitive out of the gate with strong performance on track.

“Formula E is important for Citroen strategically as it provides the opportunity to push electric technologies through competition which, in turn, will make future Citroen Road cars better. I am excited to be aligned with Citroën because it is a brand for all people, and I love the fact that our fans can support the team on track while having a Citroën as part of their everyday lives. Racing, technology and that connection with people all come together here, and that makes this project very special.”

A new challenge for Fred Espinos

This new role of Deputy Team Principal at Citroën Racing comes after Espinos, who has progressed up through the championship having started as Sporting Manager with ABT Sportsline and will now help with the iconic French manufacturer as a new era begins.

Espinos, who was chosen to represent his former Lola Yamaha ABT team on the Shanghai podium when Lucas di Grassi snatched a shock victory earlier this year, this is an opportunity that feels like the right challenge at the right time.

“I’m very proud to join the team at such an important stage in its development,” he said. “This is a project that brings together many of the ingredients needed to succeed: a brand with a strong motorsport heritage, an experienced team, two top-level drivers and a clear ambition as we enter the GEN4 era. I’m very happy to bring my Formula E experience to this group and to work alongside Beth and the entire team. We have a lot of work ahead of us, but the objective is clear: to be ready from the very start of the season.”

Who will be driving for Citroën Racing?

Both Nick Cassidy and Jean-Eric Vergne are already confirmed to be returning to their roles as full-time drivers for the Citroën Racing team in the 2026/27 season – the first of the thrilling new GEN4 era.

The two drivers, with 23 wins between them across their respective time in the all-electric championship, are one of the most experienced duos on the grid.

In their – and the team’s – first season in Formula E, they both achieved podiums and Cassidy delivered the team a victory in just their second single-seater race at the 2026 Mexico City E-Prix.

They’re now ready for a new challenge as the championship enters its new GEN4 era, with new cars, circuits and teams entering the world of Formula E electric racing.

title: World's first Formula E karting experience in Abha fuels Saudi Arabia's motorsport future
excerpt:
Three weeks from opening, the pioneering indoor attraction at SEVEN Abha has already seen thousands of guests as Saudi residents and visitors experience the world's only Formula E-branded karting destination.

Three weeks following the opening of Saudi Entertainment Ventures’ (SEVEN) landmark entertainment destination in Abha, Formula E today celebrates the flying start of Formula E Karting at SEVEN Abha - the first-ever karting attraction in the world to carry the prestigious Formula E name.

Located in the heart of the Aseer Region, Formula E Karting features as one of several entertainment zones within SEVEN Abha. This groundbreaking indoor karting experience is officially open, turning spectators into drivers and rapidly becoming a major hub for grassroots motorsport and family entertainment in the Kingdom.

Developed under an official license from Formula E, the attraction translates the championship's sustainable racing DNA into an adrenaline-fueled, 428-meter indoor track. The venue boasts a cutting-edge fleet of adult, junior, and dual electric karts, navigating guests through highly immersive, technology-driven racing zones and multi-sensory lighting.

Off the track, visitors can explore interactive heritage displays tracing the rich history of Formula E's drivers, teams, and technical innovations, alongside key environmental messages that reflect the sport's founding purpose as a proving ground for electric vehicle (EV) performance.

This world-first attraction aligns seamlessly with the goals of Saudi Vision 2030, enriching the quality of life for Saudi citizens and residents while cultivating a passionate, new generation of local motorsport talent. By placing this global first in Abha, Formula E and SEVEN are expanding premium leisure and sport experiences beyond major metropolitan hubs into the vibrant Aseer Region. Abha is the first of four SEVEN entertainment destinations in Saudi Arabia to feature a Formula E Karting attraction, with additional attractions already in development in Riyadh (Al Hamra), Dammam and Al Kharj.

Jeff Dodds, CEO, Formula E said: "We are pleased to partner with SEVEN to create Formula E’s first-ever karting experience. As a unique touchpoint for our sport, we hope the immersive nature of the attraction can serve as an opportunity to introduce and educate new audiences about Formula E, helping support the strong growth in fandom we have witnessed in the region in recent years.”

Essam Aljubair, COO of SEVEN, said: “Opening the world’s first Formula E Karting experience at SEVEN Abha marks an important milestone in our commitment to bringing distinctive, accessible entertainment experiences to

communities across Saudi Arabia. Through this partnership, families and motorsport enthusiasts can enjoy an interactive experience that combines excitement and technology while expanding entertainment choices and supporting quality of life in the Aseer Region, We also hope these tracks can help discover and develop Saudi talent, and that one day we will see a Saudi driver competing in Formula E.”

The launch of Formula E Karting in Abha arrives at a historic moment for motorsport in the Kingdom. title: Mitch Evans: “I'm at a stage in my career where I'm used to winning, and I don't want that to stop.”
excerpt:
After a decade with Jaguar, Mitch Evans is set to show up with Formula E newcomers Opel GSE next season, making it one of the biggest driver moves ahead of the GEN4 era.

During his decade in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship, Mitch Evans has been synonymous with Jaguar TCS Racing, achieving 16 victories, 38 podiums, and 10 pole positions with the British-based squad. As of the end of the 2025/26 season, the New Zealander has won the most races of any driver in the history of the all-electric championship.

The 32-year-old was also the first driver to bring home silverware for the iconic manufacturer, when he crossed the line third at the Hong Kong E-Prix in 2017. The following season, he went one step further by claiming victory in Rome, securing both his and Jaguar’s first triumph in the all-electric series.

NEWS: Opel finalises 2026/27 line-up with Mitch Evans signing

Evans has consistently delivered promising performances and has rarely been out of title contention since those early seasons. He joined Formula E at 22 years old, having just come off a GP2 series campaign in which he totalled five wins and 13 podiums - his success in the series following his championship winning GP3 season in 2012.

His arrival in the Formula E paddock would ultimately become the start of a long career, one that helped shape Evans both professionally and personally.

“I've got some more grey hair since I joined Formula E with Jaguar," he jokes. "But as a driver, as a person, we all grow older. I've been really fortunate to grow with them and the championship.

“Being in Formula E during that period has really helped me and challenged me. I look at things differently now, which obviously always comes with age. As a driver, it's really challenged me from a technical point of view, thinking outside the box, which is what Formula E is about when it comes to developing systems and software, which are areas that I never had growing up.

“Formula E is not all about going as fast as possible. There's a lot of aspects to that, it's really strengthened the way I view the championship in terms of racing and getting the most out of it. I've had some amazing memories and achievements, but some difficult periods where I've missed out on championships. I think you learn a lot about yourself in those situations, the good and bad. I'm a better driver or person than I was 10 years ago, which is the main thing, and I’m still hungry to succeed more.”

Hunger for success has always been one of Evans' greatest traits, and one that has been particularly evident in recent seasons. He has twice finished runner-up in the Drivers’ Championship, in Season 9 and Season 11, while he finished third in Season 8 and (most recently) Season 12. His latest title challenge came this year, when the New Zealander entered the London finale weekend as one of nine drivers mathematically in title contention heading into the final double-header, before the fight narrowed down to three on Sunday - Evans included.

The first half of the round saw Evans take eighth in qualifying, while his title rivals, Andretti’s Jake Dennis and Porsche's Pascal Wehrlein lined up fifth and on Pole Position, respectively. Wehrlein made the perfect start from the front of the grid, while teammate Nico Muller kept Evans behind him.

The Porsche driver capitalised on a late Full Course Yellow to take victory, adding 28 points to his tally as Dennis followed him in second. Evans, meanwhile, was left with nothing but frustration as the result left him 21 points behind in the standings.

Sunday, the final race of the GEN3 era, presented Evans with one final opportunity. Victory was the only result that would give him a realistic chance of overturning his deficit, following his costly result in the previous race.

He qualified fifth, while Wehrlein started third and Dennis could only manage 16th in his lime-green car. However, despite his best efforts, Evans was unable to produce the result he needed, finishing the race in fourth. This result left him third in the final drivers' standings with 160 points.

NEWS: Pascal Wehrlein wins his second Formula E Drivers' World Championship

But there was a silver lining, as Evans still managed to help Jaguar TCS Racing secure their second Teams’ Championship title, alongside his teammate, Antonio Felix da Costa, rounding up a total of 288 points - a final gift to the team who have played such a key role in his Formula E story.

As the championship prepares to kickstart the GEN4 era, it's most exciting era to date, Evans admits that he’s ready for a new challenge, though it means leaving a team he’s built a career and life with. “Obviously coming off the back of London, with mixed emotions. On one hand missing out on the driver's championship, and on the other hand, leaving a team that I've been with for 10 years. It was a strange feeling.

“GEN4 was a big reason why I wanted to move. I decided that I will look elsewhere, and there was some good interest from a lot of top teams. I have considered it in the past, and it's not the first time I've considered leaving Jaguar, although it's the first time I've really acted on it, I was with one team for so long, and you are always intrigued to see what other offers are out there or what other teams are up to.

“From the initial chats with Jörg (Schrott) and everyone at Opel, I felt really positive about their approach to Formula E. I visited their facilities in Satory, which really helped me, in terms of seeing their vision, seeing their resources, and seeing how seriously they're going to take the GEN4.

NEWS: Opel announces entry into Formula E from 2026/27 season

“For me it was relatively new territory for me to go down this route with another team. Opel is going to be a new team, a new brand coming to Formula E, but we have got high hopes and aspirations to hit the ground running come the season starting. I was filled with confidence, although there's an element you don't really know how it's going to go, but that comes with any decision you make.”

While the move represents a significant change for Evans, his new teammate, Theo Pourchaire is hardly an unknown quantity in motorsport. Pourchaire was crowned FIA Formula 2 champion in 2023 after finishing runner-up in the 2022 standings behind Felipe Drugovich.

“I've obviously never worked with Theo (Pourchaire) before," Evans says. "He's a few years younger than me. He's coming into Formula E at a similar age to when I did. But look, Theo's track record speaks for itself, he's had amazing success in junior formula. He was the youngest winner in F3, at 16, and he beat me by 4 days when he was in F3. I have to have a word with him about that.

“He's achieved some amazing things, and he deserves this opportunity. It's an exciting partnership because he's a rookie on paper, but he's going to come in with fresh energy, and prove himself. He's going to add a lot of value. and then obviously on my side, you've got the older guy, which is kind of weird to say, but I think he's not going to need much help in terms of getting up to speed. I'm expecting really big things from him.”

NEWS: Théo Pourchaire joins Formula E grid with Opel GSE Formula E Team

Evans had been through three generations of Formula E cars and demonstrated an ability to adapt to the championship’s constantly evolving technology. Even so, he is approaching his first season with Opel GSE with realistic expectations.

“I'm not setting any crazy targets," he says. "But we're pushing to be able to achieve podiums and ideally race wins in our first season, that'd be amazing. Do I think we can achieve it? Yes, but it's too early to say, it's a bit of a punt.

“The early signs have been really positive in terms of testing and what we're seeing amongst other teams we've been testing. We're in good shape, but there's a lot of development and a lot of things that can happen between now and the first race or throughout the season. There will be a massive development race, while we learn these cars.

“If we can keep development up, then I'm quite confident that we'll be ideally fighting at the front. I wouldn't be jumping to Opel if I didn't think that was possible. I'm at a stage in my career, where I'm used to winning, and I don't want that to stop.”

title: Formula E unveils bold new identity as it accelerates into next era
excerpt:
Formula E introduces a bold, progressive brand identity that turns Formula E's ambition to 'Make Progress Thrilling’ into a faster, more visceral experience.

Formula E today unveiled a dynamic new brand identity, signalling a decisive evolution as the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship enters its next era.

The timing coincides with the revolutionary GEN4 race car debuting in December, its biggest global calendar to date, a landmark streaming partnership with Disney+, and a new high-stakes E-PrixUnleashed format. Formula E is shifting gears; and has built a visual identity to match.

The evolved identity signals a decisive shift in how Formula E presents itself to the world. The brand now delivers a confident statement on what high-performance, sustainable racing is today.

Formula E is electric motorsport without compromise.

Built for a dynamic landscape of live sport, streaming, social, and gaming, the update is deliberately kinetic. Its visual language channels forward surge, speed, and constant motion, blending the raw competitive DNA of motorsport with the immediacy of contemporary culture.

The result is a brand that refuses to sit neatly in its lane.

At the center of the visual update is an angular, motion-led logomark featuring hidden "F" and "E" design elements that communicate forward movement and speed. The broader system includes updated broadcast graphics designed to improve viewing clarity during high-speed, wheel-to-wheel battles.

As a challenger brand, Formula E set out to create something unique with real standout, aiming to sit between motorsport and contemporary culture by blurring and reflecting the relentless momentum and enduring pursuit of progress that sits at the heart of the Championship and is shared by its global fans.

A NEW VISUAL IDENTITY

The visual identity is structured around five core strategic pillars:

● Speed, Technology and Competition: Highlighting extreme performance, technical sophistication, and close wheel-to-wheel racing.

● Cultural Relevance: Designed to show up in culture, not just motorsport, from social and streaming to gaming, live events, fashion and beyond.

● Purpose Driven by Performance: Re-framing sustainability not as a compromise, but as a primary engine for speed, innovation, and technological breakthrough.

● Evolution for Loyal Fans: Retaining foundational values-innovation, progress, and competition-while carrying them into a more modern, expressive platform.

● Platform for Partners and Host Cities: Providing flexible, ownable brand assets for sponsors, manufacturers, and host cities to build deeper connections with younger, culturally engaged audiences.

Ellie Norman, Chief Marketing Officer Formula E, said: “Formula E is growing rapidly across every dimension; from the racing on track to our global audience and commercial partnerships. Our previous identity represented an earlier chapter; this brand refresh reflects exactly where we are going next.

We believe progress should be thrilling. We are no longer asking people to imagine what the future of racing could be, we are showing them what it looks like. It is fast, competitive, technologically advanced and culturally relevant, and we want the world to experience it that way.”

The brand architecture spans a modernised logo, refined typography, dynamic color palettes, high-energy motion graphics, and an evolved broadcast package designed to look as alive on a phone screen as it does at 200 mph on track.

Bold colours and expressive typography capture the relentless and dynamic energy and the result is a more expressive and recognisable Formula E world across every fan touchpoint.

For core motorsport fans, the evolution retains the foundational values of innovation and competition that have defined Formula E since its inception. The Championship continues to serve as a vital competitive ground for world-leading automotive manufacturers including Porsche, Jaguar, Nissan, Stellantis, Mahindra, and Lola Cars.
